subject: Operations
title: Ericsson and the Philips Fire
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Ericsson and the Philips Fire.

hook.text: A 10-minute fire at a Philips chip plant cost Ericsson $400 million. Nokia, using the same plant, lost nothing.

buildup.text: In 2000, lightning struck a Philips semiconductor plant in New Mexico. A small fire contaminated millions of chips.

discovery.text: Both Ericsson and Nokia sourced radio frequency chips from that plant. Philips told both the delay would be short.

twist.text: Nokia escalated fast—sourcing chips from Japan and redesigning alternatives. Ericsson waited and trusted Philips.

climax.text: Nokia barely missed a beat. Ericsson couldn't make phones for months and exited the handset business two years later.

punchline.text: Same disaster. Different responses. Opposite outcomes.

quiz.question: Why did Nokia survive the Philips fire while Ericsson didn't?
